Rotorless Flying Saucer powered by an EM Field and its flight method  - China patent 

#ufotwitter

Patent was filed on December 31, 2019, by inventors Meng Jun and Yu Huize from Zhejiang University 

The patent describes a disc-shaped (flying saucer) aircraft that achieves lift and propulsion without any rotors, propellers, jets, or combustion engines. Instead, it relies entirely on electromagnetic fields to ionize air and create directed ion flows for thrust and lift.

Key components:

Control unit (typically ground-based, e.g., a mobile terminal/smartphone): Inputs commands, plans paths using GPS/3D maps, sends tasks, and monitors status.

Analysis unit (onboard): Processes commands, uses sensors (gyroscope, accelerometer, GPS/Beidou, ultrasonic, optical flow, pressure sensors), and provides real-time feedback on attitude, position, speed, height, and obstacles.

Execution unit (onboard propulsion system):

Lift module: Central ion generators (high-voltage electrodes) paired with coils. Creates rotating ion flows using electric fields (to ionize/accelerate air) and magnetic fields (Lorentz force to curve ion paths). This generates a negative pressure/vacuum effect above or below the saucer for vertical lift.

Horizontal power module: Multiple pairs of ion generators evenly distributed around the edges. Produces directional ion flows for forward/backward/sideways thrust.

How It Works (Core Principle)

1. High-voltage electrodes ionize surrounding air into charged particles (ions).
2. Electric fields accelerate these ions.
3. Magnetic fields (from coils) influence ion paths, creating rotation or directed flows.
4. The moving ion clouds induce pressure differences (lower pressure in the flow direction), generating lift or thrust via aerodynamic effects — similar in concept to ion wind or electrohydrodynamic (EHD) thrust, but enhanced with rotating magnetic control.

Patent tie in to - Nazi Germany Haunebu flying saucer

Before anyone ask yes this patent fully resembles long rumoured Nazi Germany Haunebu flying saucer which some claim first prototype was made in 1928 make you wonder even more how far back we knew about advanced/unconventional propulsion systems. 

This same looking vehicle was sighted in 1966 over Hillsdale college, United States and photographed vehicle was called chicken feeder by J. Allen Hynek.

It's pretty ironic that China state body Zhejiang University patented what was once called by J. Allen Hynek chicken feeder or swamp gas.
